Being out of high school for about ten years, here is how I did it:

I wenh to the library, picked up a math book, and started reading the instructional pages and doing some of the practice problems. Most books will have answers in the back (usually for the odd questions) for you to check your work. Approach it like lifting weights, and start with something you're confident doing, and move up at your own speed. You don't need to do EVERY problem, but don't skip any of the sections. You'll be surprised at what you've forgotten.

You can also join a forum for creative writing. Just write something (which you'll probably think is shitty, and not want to post), post it, and listen to the criticism. It's important you find a legitimate forum, since some of the "social media" forums are full of children who will berate you without giving you constructive criticism. You want someone who knows how to write, and who loves reading good material, telling you what they didn't like about your work.

This is what I did, and when I went back to school, it was easy for me. I attribute that to keeping up with my works, and not being lazy.
